t: An island kingdom united by Kamehameha I between 1795 and 1810, with its capital at Lahaina from 1820 and at Honolulu from 1845.
It became a constitutional monarchy in 1840, and Britain and France recognised its independence in 1843.
Planters forced the Bayonet Constitution on Kalākaua in 1887, and a committee backed by US troops overthrew Liliʻuokalani in 1893.
dyk: ʻIolani Palace in Honolulu was lit by electricity by 1887, four years before electric lighting was installed in the White House in Washington in 1891.
ev: Kamehameha I wins the Battle of Nuʻuanu and takes Oʻahu
Kaumualiʻi of Kauaʻi accepts Kamehameha as overlord, completing unification
The kapu system is abolished after the death of Kamehameha I
Kamehameha III grants the kingdom’s first constitution
Britain and France jointly recognise Hawaiian independence
The Great Māhele divides the kingdom’s land
Kalākaua is forced to sign the Bayonet Constitution
Queen Liliʻuokalani is overthrown and a Provisional Government proclaimed

f.capital: Royal seats at Kailua-Kona and Honolulu under Kamehameha I; Lahaina (1820–1845); Honolulu (1845–1893)
f.predecessor: Chiefdoms of Hawaiʻi Island, Maui, Oʻahu and Kauaʻi
f.successor: Provisional Government of Hawaii (1893), then the Republic of Hawaii (1894)
